output.subject: Your question about options for your September car payment
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for getting in touch, and for reaching out ahead of your due date. You told us your work hours were cut in half in August, and that with your car payment of $452.60 due on September 21, you expect to be able to cover about a third of it. You also mentioned that you have never been late in four years. You would like to know what your options are, including whether a payment plan could be set up, before things become harder to manage.

We're sorry you're dealing with this change in your income. We know it can be a stressful time. We have passed your question to our Consumer Lending team, who will review your situation and the options you asked about. They will respond within 10 business days.

If anything changes in the meantime, or if there is more you would like us to know about your circumstances, please reply to this email and we will add it to your request.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: This is a hardship question rather than a complaint; the customer is asking for options before missing a payment.
Check today's date against the September 21 due date. A 10-business-day response may arrive after the payment is due, so consider earlier contact from Consumer Lending.
Decide which hardship or payment plan options, if any, to offer. The draft does not commit to any.
Confirm what happens if a partial payment is made by September 21, such as late fees or credit reporting, before advising the customer.
Verify the loan account, the $452.60 payment amount, the due date and the customer's four-year on-time payment history.
Consider whether to say anything about making the partial payment they can afford in the meantime. The draft deliberately does not advise on this.
